title: Design Add And Search Words Data Structure
description: Store words and search patterns where a dot matches any one character.
note: Walk literal characters iteratively, branching recursively only at a wildcard.
notes: TrieNode belongs to the solution rather than the problem's provided types. WordDictionary uses methods on a record with a fresh default root; addWord is a procedure, and search returns bool.

map(TrieNode) creates children only during insertion. Literal search uses get(char), which returns none without inserting or invoking that factory. The bool-returning matcher explicitly returns false on a miss rather than propagating none with ?.

matches is a separate function because its state arrives through parameters. It iterates literal characters from start, preserving the trie position, and recurses only when a dot chooses among child nodes. A dot consumes exactly one Unicode scalar value.

any evaluates boolean predicates lazily, stops at the first true result, and returns false for an empty source. node.chars.values() still constructs its complete snapshot first; short-circuiting avoids later recursive searches, not that snapshot allocation. Map value order remains unspecified, but the boolean answer is independent of that order.

After the pattern is exhausted, node.isEnd distinguishes a full word from an unfinished prefix. Duplicate insertion is harmless, while patterns that are too short or too long fail unless a word with that exact length exists.

Fixtures run ordered method calls against one fresh object per case, checking literal and wildcard queries before and after insertion, shared prefixes, failed searches, and repeated additions. JSON null represents a procedure call's completion in the fixture protocol.

Insertion takes expected O(L) work and at most O(L) new nodes for L characters. A search without wildcards takes expected O(L) work. Wildcards may explore every matching trie branch; with maximum branching B and w wildcards, O(L * B^w) is a coarse upper bound for B >= 1. Recursion depth is at most L, and live values snapshots add storage for the children examined at active wildcard levels.
